\subsection*{Randomized --- ZPPHosts: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Repeated-round halting probability bound]
\lean{Randomized.randProb_rounds_le}
\label{Randomized.randProb_rounds_le}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_append_le, Randomized.randProb_congr, Randomized.randProb_le_one, Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_of_halt}
\difficulty{6}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean input and
work-tape symbols, and state set $\mathrm{St}$, and let $\mathrm{Ready}$ be a predicate
on configurations for a fixed Boolean input $x$. Fix a round length $R\in\mathbb N$ and
a rational $a\ge 0$. Suppose that from every ready configuration, every choice word of
length $R$ leads either to a halted configuration or to another ready configuration; and
suppose that from every ready configuration, the probability of halting after a
uniformly chosen length-$R$ choice word is at most $a$. Then for every $j\in\mathbb N$
and every ready configuration $c$, the probability that the machine halts after a
uniformly chosen choice word of length $Rj$ is at most $a^j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rounds until a halted run satisfies a property]
\lean{Randomized.halted_rounds}
\label{Randomized.halted_rounds}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_of_halt}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean input, and
state set $S$. Let $R$ be a natural number, and let $P$ and $	ext{Ready}$ be properties
of configurations on a fixed Boolean input. Suppose that from every ready configuration,
every choice word of length $R$ leads either to a halted configuration satisfying $P$,
or to another ready configuration. Suppose also that every ready configuration is
nonhalted. Then, for every natural number $j$, every ready initial configuration, and
every choice word of length $Rj$, if the resulting run is halted, its final
configuration satisfies $P$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expected Nonhalting Bound from Round Decay]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.expTimeLe_of_rounds}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.expTimeLe_of_rounds}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.notHaltedProb, Randomized.notHaltedProb_le_one, Randomized.notHaltedProb_nonneg, Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_congr, Randomized.randProb_split, Randomized.randProb_true, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.ExpTimeLe, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun_eq_none_iff, Turing.FinNDTM.notHaltedProb_haltRun_antitone, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append}
\difficulty{6}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let
$x$ be a binary input, and let $s_0,R\in\mathbb{N}$ with $R>0$. Suppose there is a
configuration $c_0$ such that every choice word of length $s_0$ reaches $c_0$ from the
initial configuration on $x$. Let $a\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0\le a<1$, and suppose that
for every $j\in\mathbb{N}$ the probability that a uniformly chosen length-$Rj$ choice
word leaves the run from $c_0$ unhalted is at most $a^j$. Then, for every
$K\in\mathbb{N}$, the sum over $t=0,\ldots,K-1$ of the probability that a uniformly
chosen length-$t$ choice word leaves the run from the initial configuration on $x$
unhalted is at most $s_0+R/(1-a)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of time bounds]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.ZDecidesInTime.mono}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.ZDecidesInTime.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM.ZDecidesInTime}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $L$ be a
language of Boolean words, and let $T_1,T_2\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. If $N$ has
total nonhalting probability at most $T_1(|x|)$ on every input $x$ and every halted run
outputs the one-symbol indicator of whether $x\in L$, and if $T_1(n)\le T_2(n)$ for
every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, then $N$ has total nonhalting probability at most $T_2(|x|)$ on
every input and retains the same output condition on every halted run.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of aborting decision time]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.AbortDecidesInTime.mono}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.AbortDecidesInTime.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM.AbortDecidesInTime, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb_eq_of_haltsWithin, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith, Turing.FinNDTM.runWith_eq_runWith_take, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin.mono}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, $L$ a
language of binary strings, and $T_1,T_2:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ time bounds. Suppose
that on every input $x$, every branch of $N$ halts after $T_1(|x|)$ choices, no such
branch outputs the one-bit string encoding the complement of membership in $L$, and the
probability of outputting the one-bit membership value is at least $1/2$. If $T_1(n)\le
T_2(n)$ for every $n$, then the same guarantees hold with time bound $T_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Attempted output bit]
\lean{Randomized.attemptBit}
\label{Randomized.attemptBit}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.bitOfOutput, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun}
Given a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $A$ over the Boolean alphabet and Boolean
lists $x$ and $u$, the attempted bit is the bit extracted from the machine's halted run
on $x$ with auxiliary input $u$, if that run yields an extractable bit; otherwise it is
undefined.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{4}
Let $A$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine, and let $x,u$ be bit strings and
$v$ a bit. The attempt on input $x$ with choice string $u$ returns $v$ exactly when the
run halts and outputs the one-bit string $v$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Clocked Zero-Error Decision with Expected-Time Bound]
\lean{Randomized.clockHost_zDecides}
\label{Randomized.clockHost_zDecides}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.attemptBit, Randomized.attemptBit_eq_some, Randomized.halted_rounds, Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_mono, Randomized.randProb_rounds_le, Randomized.randProb_take, Turing.Cfg, Turing.ClockHost.ClockReady, Turing.ClockHost.ClockReady.state_ne_none, Turing.ClockHost.hostTM, Turing.ClockHost.readyAt_initCfg, Turing.ClockHost.round, Turing.ClockHost.runCfg, Turing.ClockHost.startup, Turing.ClockPhase, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.ZDecidesInTime, Turing.FinNDTM.clockHost, Turing.FinNDTM.expTimeLe_of_rounds, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_of_halt}
\difficulty{6}
Let $S$ be a finite-state deterministic machine, $A$ a finite-state nondeterministic
machine, $L$ a language of Boolean words, and $m,T_S:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose
$S$ computes the all-true word of length $m(|x|)$ on every input $x$ within $T_S(|x|)$
steps, and $n\le m(n)$ for every $n$. Suppose every length-$m(|x|)$ witness on which an
attempt by $A$ on $x$ halts with a single output bit yields the correct membership
indicator, and that for every $x$ the probability that a uniformly random
length-$m(|x|)$ witness does not yield such a bit is at most $3/4$. Then the clocked
host machine built from $S$ and $A$ with its looping option enabled has cumulative
nonhalting probability at most $T_S(n)+m(n)+2+16(m(n)+1)$: for every natural number $K$,
the sum over $t<K$ of the probability that it has not halted after $t$ steps is at most
this bound. Every witness on which it halts produces exactly the one-bit membership
indicator of $L$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $S$ be a finite-state deterministic machine, $A$ a finite-state nondeterministic
machine, $L$ a language of Boolean words, and $m,T_S:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose
$S$ computes the all-true word of length $m(|x|)$ on every input $x$ within $T_S(|x|)$
steps, and $n\le m(n)$ for every $n$. Suppose also that for every $x,u,v$, if
$|u|=m(|x|)$ and the attempt by $A$ on $x$ with witness $u$ halts with a single output
bit $v$, then $v$ equals the Boolean indicator of whether $x\in L$; and, for every $x$,
a uniformly random Boolean word $u$ of length $m(|x|)$ yields that correct bit with
probability at least $1/2$. Then the clocked host machine built from $S$ and $A$ with
its looping option disabled decides $L$ within $T_S(n)+m(n)+2+(m(n)+1)$ steps: it halts
on every witness, never outputs the incorrect bit, and outputs the correct bit with
probability at least $1/2$.
\end{theorem}
